meta.title: Social Organizer — assistance begins with coordinated action
meta.description: Social Organizer helps participants report Needs and voluntary Participation. Participants make their own decisions, and assistance happens directly between them. Open source, a non-profit project.

hero.title: Assistance begins with coordinated action
hero.lead: Social Organizer helps participants report Needs and voluntary Participation. Participants make their own decisions, and assistance happens directly between them.
hero.sceneAria: A Need travels by handshakes, participants report Participation

steps.title: How it works
steps.lead: Four steps. At each one the participant decides for themselves.
steps.s1Text: A Need is the first of two signals. It says how much is needed and where to get in touch: an amount and a chat link.
steps.s2Title: Others learn of it and decide for themselves
steps.s2Text: The message travels by handshakes: first to people the participant knows in person, then to the people they know. Everyone decides for themselves whether they can assist.
steps.s3Text: Participation is the second signal: a voluntary intention, not a payment.
steps.s4Title: Actions happen directly, outside Social Organizer
steps.s4Text: What to do and how, participants agree and carry out directly with each other, in their own chat.

chain.title: A Need travels by handshakes
chain.lead: You see Maria’s Need because Oleg knows her, and you know Oleg. You may leave the message unanswered. No obligations.

nots.title: What Social Organizer does not do
nots.moneyText: It does not accept, transfer or hold funds. Whatever participants do, they do directly, outside the service.
nots.feeText: Open source, a non-profit project. No subscription, no ads, no percentage.
nots.choiceText: Whom to add, whether to take part and how — it is your choice every time. Saying no breaks nothing.

principles.title: Principles
principles.p1Text: Nobody has to respond. Participation is a decision, not a debt.
principles.p2Text: Everyone decides for themselves, with no organiser and no scores. Declining carries no sanction.
principles.p3Text: Arrangements and actions stay between people linked by confirmed acquaintance.
principles.p4Text: Two signals and notifications about them. No centralised distribution.

faq.title: The essentials
faq.a1: It records two signals, Need and Participation, and provides the feedback connected with them. It does not act on behalf of participants.
faq.q2: Do I have to take part?
faq.a2: No. Participation is voluntary, and everyone makes their own decision.
faq.a3: No. The outcome depends on the independent decisions and actual actions of participants.
faq.a4: No. Social Organizer does not accept, transfer or hold funds. Anything participants do between themselves, they do directly, outside the service.
faq.a5: They may. A Need names an amount, and a Participation names how much a participant is ready to hand over. If participants hand over money, they do it themselves and directly, by their own arrangement. Social Organizer does not verify whether a handover took place.
faq.a6: In US dollars: a common unit of account, so that amounts can be compared. Which currency and which way to use is up to participants.

meta.title: How it works — Social Organizer
meta.description: Two signals, Need and Participation: how a message travels by handshakes and why actions happen directly between participants.

hero.title: Two signals and a direct connection
hero.lead: Social Organizer has only two signals. A Need is a participant’s message about what they need. A Participation is another participant’s message about their own voluntary participation. Everything else people agree and do themselves, directly.

table.title: A historical example: the hui
table.lead: In southern China six friends put in a share once a month, and one of them takes that month’s shares. Tap a month or a name.
says: Lin takes January’s shares. Five friends put in a share each.
Chen takes February’s shares. Lin puts in a share too.
Mei takes March’s shares. Chen puts in a share too.
Guo takes April’s shares. Mei puts in a share too.
Sun takes May’s shares. Guo puts in a share too.
Huang takes June’s shares. The circle is closed: everyone got it once.
table.note: This is an example of voluntary assistance between people who know each other, not how Social Organizer is built: it has no common pot, no queue and no required shares.

orbit.title: How far a message travels
orbit.lead: Your friends know their own, and a Need travels by handshakes. It reaches those who have a path to you through people they know, and everyone decides for themselves.
says: Six people you know. This is the circle: people you have confirmed you know.
Each of the six has their own six. 36 people you do not know, but someone of yours does.
One more step — 216 people. The message reaches them too, through those who know you.
orbit.sumNote: if everyone named {{share}}. A simplified example: in life circles overlap, and nobody has to take part

policy.s1: Social Organizer ("we", "our", "the service") is an open-source coordination tool: it carries participants’ messages about Needs and voluntary Participation. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, and protect your personal data when you use the app, our Telegram Mini App and the website at orginizer.com.
policy.s2a: Account data: name, email address, Telegram user ID and username (when logging in via Telegram).
policy.s2b: Profile data: photo, contact information you choose to add (social links, phone number).
policy.s2c: Network data: your connections with other users, invitation history.
policy.s2d: Activity data: Needs you report, your Participation, the amounts you name, and your minimum participation.
policy.s3a: To run the service: to show you the network of people you know.
policy.s3b: To carry messages about Needs and Participation across your network.
policy.s3c: To send notifications about Needs, invitations, and network activity.
policy.s3d: To improve the App based on aggregated, anonymized usage patterns.
policy.s4lead: We do not sell your personal data. Your data is shared only with:
policy.s4a: Your network members: your name, photo, and contact info you choose to make visible.
policy.s4b: Telegram: data necessary for the Mini App to function within Telegram.
policy.s4c: Hosting providers: our servers process your data to deliver the service.
policy.s5: Your data is stored in a secure PostgreSQL database. We use encrypted connections (HTTPS/TLS), JWT-based authentication, and follow industry-standard security practices to protect your information. Accounts with no sign-ins for 2 years are deleted automatically, after notices 30 and 7 days in advance.
policy.s6a: Access your personal data through your profile and settings.
policy.s6b: Correct or update your information at any time.
policy.s6c: Delete your account and associated data yourself in Profile → Account.
policy.s6d: Export your data in a machine-readable format.
policy.s7: Social Organizer is fully open source. You can review our codebase and how your data is handled at <gh>github.com/element1965/Social-organizer</gh>.
policy.s8: For questions about this Privacy Policy or your data, contact us via <bot>Telegram</bot>.
policy.s3e: To decide who receives a Need first: we count how often you open and answer such messages, and how many you got lately. These counts are never shown to anyone and used for nothing else.

termsDoc.s1: Social Organizer is a free, open-source coordination tool. It records two kinds of participant messages, a Need and a voluntary Participation, and notifies people about them. The service is available in the app, as a Telegram Mini App and at orginizer.com.
termsDoc.s2: By using Social Organizer, you agree to these Terms of Service. If you do not agree, please do not use the App.
termsDoc.s3a: You must provide accurate information when creating an account.
termsDoc.s3b: You are responsible for maintaining the security of your account.
termsDoc.s3c: You may create only one account per person.
termsDoc.s3d: You must be at least 16 years old to use the service.
termsDoc.s4a: Confirm that they know each other through personal invitations.
termsDoc.s4b: Report a Need and their own voluntary Participation.
termsDoc.s4d: Discover connection paths between network members.
termsDoc.s5a: Report invented Needs or mislead other people.
termsDoc.s5b: Misrepresent your identity or relationship to others.
termsDoc.s5c: Use the service for illegal activities or spam.
termsDoc.s5d: Attempt to exploit, hack, or disrupt the service.
termsDoc.s6: Social Organizer is a coordination tool, not a financial institution, a fund or a payment intermediary. The service does not accept, transfer, hold or distribute funds. A Participation is a participant’s voluntary intention; it is not a payment. Participants may agree to hand over money or to help in another way: such arrangements and actions take place directly between them, outside the service. Amounts and received marks are entered by participants themselves; the service does not verify them. We do not guarantee that assistance will be given and are not responsible for whether participants keep their arrangements.
termsDoc.s7: The service is provided "as is" without warranties of any kind. We are not liable for any damages arising from the use of the service, including but not limited to financial losses from arrangements between participants that were not kept.
termsDoc.s8: Social Organizer is open-source software licensed under its repository terms. The source code is available at <gh>github.com/element1965/Social-organizer</gh>.
termsDoc.s9a: Social Organizer has a zero-tolerance policy toward child sexual abuse and exploitation (CSAE). We strictly prohibit any content, behavior, or use of the service that sexually exploits or endangers minors in any way.

termsDoc.s9b: Sharing, distributing, or soliciting child sexual abuse material (CSAM) of any kind.
termsDoc.s9c: Grooming, trafficking, or exploitation of minors.
termsDoc.s9d: Any communication of a sexual nature with or about minors.
termsDoc.s9e: Using the service to facilitate access to children for harmful purposes.
termsDoc.s9f: Users must be at least 16 years of age. We reserve the right to immediately terminate accounts and report violators to the appropriate law enforcement authorities, including the <ncmec>National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC)</ncmec> and local law enforcement.
termsDoc.s9g: If you encounter any content or behavior that violates these standards, please report it immediately via <bot>Telegram</bot>.
termsDoc.s10: We may update these terms from time to time. Continued use of the App after changes constitutes acceptance of the new terms.
termsDoc.s11: For questions about these Terms, contact us via <bot>Telegram</bot>.
